hints: Same distance, same time. Write each car’s distance in time T and set them equal; then T follows, and the range from either car.
worded:
1. Both cars cover the race length R in the same time T, starting together.

2. Setting u₁T + ½αT² equal to u₂T + ½βT² and cancelling one T gives T = 2(u₁ − u₂)/(β − α). The car with the higher start speed must have the lower acceleration for this to be positive.

3. Put this T back into either car’s distance to get R.

**Another way: relative motion.** In car 2’s frame, car 1 starts at relative speed u₁ − u₂ with relative acceleration −(β − α). It returns to “level” after 2(u₁ − u₂)/(β − α), the time to go out and come back, as for a vertical throw.
conventional:
![](asset:P000122-sol-1)

$$R = u_{1}T + \frac{1}{2}\alpha T^{2} = u_{2}T + \frac{1}{2}\beta T^{2}\  \Rightarrow \ T = \frac{2\left( u_{1} - u_{2} \right)}{\beta - \alpha}.$$

$$R = T\left( u_{1} + \frac{\alpha T}{2} \right) = \frac{2\left( u_{1} - u_{2} \right)}{\beta - \alpha} \cdot \frac{u_{1}(\beta - \alpha) + \alpha\left( u_{1} - u_{2} \right)}{\beta - \alpha} = \frac{2\left( u_{1} - u_{2} \right)\left( u_{1}\beta - u_{2}\alpha \right)}{(\beta - \alpha)^{2}}.$$
mistakes: Don’t cancel T = 0: that root is the start, not the finish.
